findings.title: traceID dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' logs
findings.body: The diff removes the explicit trace correlation from logRequest (`traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` plus its append to logParams) and now relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` to populate the log record. However, the contextual attributes installed by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext` are only endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname; they do not include a trace ID. Unless `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` independently extracts the trace ID from the OTel span, the 'Plugin Request Completed' lines lose their traceID field, breaking the log/trace correlation these logs had before this PR. Verify traceID still appears and add a test that asserts it.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the injected logger, making FromContext-based logs unassertable
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns a brand-new `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver (or a logger sharing the same `Logs`). `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now emits its log via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. When a `TestLogger` is injected into the middleware, the Info call is recorded on the throwaway logger returned by FromContext, so `testLogger.InfoLogs.Calls` stays 0. Any test (existing or newly added) that asserts the middleware logged a request cannot observe it, and the moved contextual-logging behavior is effectively untestable with this fake. `FromContext` should return a logger that records into the same `Logs` as the receiver.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and moved log fields are untested
findings.body: Responsibility for endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname was moved out of LoggerMiddleware's explicit logParams into the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and the middleware ordering in pluginsintegration.go was changed (Metrics -> ContextualLogger -> Logger). There is no test for the new middleware and no test asserting those fields still appear in 'Plugin Request Completed' logs after the move. A regression in the middleware ordering or in `log.WithContextualAttributes`/`FromContext` would silently drop all these fields with no failing test. Add coverage that exercises the full chain and asserts the emitted log record contains the expected fields.

findings.title: FromContext silently drops contextual attributes on type-assertion failure
findings.body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` type-asserts the value returned by `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` to `*log.ConcreteLogger`; if the infra logger ever returns a different concrete type (for example a future wrapper around the concrete logger), the assertion fails and the method returns `d.New()`, a plain logger without the contextual attributes. Because this wrapper is now the only path by which pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname reach the backend request logs, a failed assertion would silently drop every one of those fields. Wrap the returned `log.Logger` directly (assign it to an interface-typed field) rather than asserting a concrete type, or at minimum surface the failure.
